name: Garbled or empty-sounding words still get a face
case: While an agent works, the Mac's speech recognition hands Boop words that mean nothing much: a filler, then a broken half sentence. Boop can't make sense of them, but it was spoken to, so it answers each with a face, never none, and a puzzled one (confused, baffled) is as good as any.
why: PERSONALITY: talked to, Boop always answers with a face, never none. Real transcriptions are often fragments; nothing in the words to react to mustn't mean no reaction. Words Boop can't make sense of may get the faces that say so: confused, baffled, surprised or skeptical
